channel.title: CTV News – Queen's Park
channel.description: Queen's Park coverage from CTV News Toronto.

item.title: Non-profits fear housing halt as Ontario bill targets tax exemption
Doug Ford ‘very confident’ Canada could see trade deal with U.S. soon
item.description: Ontario Premier Doug Ford and Alberta Premier Danielle Smith expressed optimism Monday that Canada could see a trade deal reached with the U.S. before the end of the year.

item.title: Minister defends not initially cutting off college with skyrocketing OSAP usage
item.description: Ontario’s minister of colleges and universities says a career college with student financial aid usage that grew thousands of per cent in a few years was not one of six he cut off in May because of the 'evolving nature of the data.'

item.title: 'Happy, exercise, help others': The secrets behind Raymond Cho's 90 years on Earth
item.description: On a recent Friday in the far eastern reaches of Toronto, Raymond Cho deftly serves a table tennis ball against a new rival, a reporter about half his age from The Canadian Press.

item.title: Navdeep Bains named new Ontario Liberal leader
item.description: Former MP Navdeep Bains eked out a narrow victory Saturday to become the next Ontario Liberal leader, pledging to focus now on uniting the party and getting it in fighting shape for the next election.

item.title: Ontario Liberals to select third new leader since 2018
item.description: Ontario Liberals wrap up a long leadership race Saturday, and, they hope, an even longer stretch without a long-term leader, as the party gets set to name the person they have selected to shepherd them into the next election.

item.title: CUPE Ontario education workers vote in favour of strike action ahead of bargaining
item.description: Ontario school board workers represented by CUPE have given their union a strike mandate, making it the fifth major education union to vote in favour of possible job action.

item.title: Northlander passenger rail service returns Dec. 10 after 14-year absence
item.description: The Northlander passenger rail service will return on Dec. 10, reconnecting Toronto and Cochrane along a route serving 16 communities after a 14-year absence. Tickets go on sale Nov. 26.

item.title: Former colleges and universities minister refuses to answer OSAP questions
item.description: Ontario’s former minister of colleges and universities, who presided over the file for three years until 2024, is refusing to answer questions about a growing Ontario Student Assistance Program scandal.

item.title: Ontario targets noisy vehicles with new steeper fines. These are the penalties drivers could face
item.description: Drivers with noisy vehicles could soon face steeper fines for blowing out eardrums as they tear down streets in Ontario.

item.title: Ontario elementary school teachers overwhelmingly vote in favour of strike mandate
item.description: The majority of members of the Elementary Teachers’ Federation of Ontario (ETFO) voted in favour of a strike action.

item.title: ‘I definitely didn’t teach him this’: Duolingo owl chirps at Doug Ford’s French
item.description: Language learning app Duolingo is clarifying that it had nothing to do with Ontario Premier Doug Ford’s tutelage after Ford’s recent comments in French drew less than complimentary reviews online.

item.title: ‘We haven’t given them any money yet’: Ontario officials hoping for good meeting with Stellantis
item.description: Ontario officials said Wednesday they’re hopeful that a meeting with the global CEO of automaker Stellantis will have a good result for the fate of some 2,200 employees who could be without jobs if a planned sale of the company’s Brampton plant goes ahead.

item.title: Ontario Premier Doug Ford touts partnerships with Quebec in Montreal speech
item.description: Ontario Premier Doug Ford says he wants to break barriers to trade between provinces and build a stronger partnership with Quebec.

item.title: Ontario secondary teachers vote 96 per cent in favour of strike mandate
item.description: Ontario public high school teachers have voted 96 per cent in favour of giving their union a strike mandate.
